entries.hypothesis: Blending the model with a multi-book consensus (instead of one book) raises Main ROI versus Baseline B without lowering the hit rate.
entries.rule: Production Main rule on p = softmax(a + b_q log q_cons + b_p log p_model) per market group, a, b fitted each month on all settled earlier matches of the season (>= 300 rows, else the model probability); q_cons = median of the de-margined (power) named books of the Football-Data snapshot for 1X2 / double chance, Football-Data average for total 2.5 and the Asian line, median of >= 2 stored books, else the single book (bet365).
entries.primary_metric: paired ROI difference vs Baseline B at the closing universe (bootstrap by match)
secondary: the same at the T universe
ROI difference vs the single-book blend (V1)
entries.minimum_forward_sample: 1000 settled bets (about 2 months of the 21 leagues)

entries.hypothesis: Using the multi-book consensus probability instead of the model probability in the production Main rule does not lower Main ROI versus Baseline B and beats the single-book market version.
entries.rule: Production Main rule on p = q_cons (as in v63-consensus-C2, handicap on the win scale with the model's refund probability); candidates without any complete book keep the model probability.
entries.primary_metric: paired ROI difference vs Baseline B at the closing universe (bootstrap by match)
secondary: the same at the T universe
ROI difference vs the single-book market version (V3)

note: B candidates frozen for a forward check on matches played after frozen_at; production is not changed.
